Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. The parent $U$ is a smooth odd divergence-free field on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, with Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$ and flow $X$. The bounds $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|D_aX\|_\infty,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$ hold. For a smooth periodic pressure $p_U$, set $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$; require $R_U$ odd, supported in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-
abla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. The formal statement imposes these conditions directly. The paper selects the zero-mean Poisson pressure; the formal statement permits any pressure meeting the displayed conditions, without separately requiring $\operatorname{div}R_U=0$.

Choose $k_*
e0$ and $0\le t_0<T$ with $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, where $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$. For each of $(D_aX)^{\pm1}$, $M=(
abla U)\circ X$, $\kappa/\lambda$, $\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2$ and $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, the formal statement bounds its $m$th label derivative by $C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$, uniformly in time and label. It also gives $|f\circ X|_m\le C_m A_f\mathsf D^{Cm}$ whenever all spatial derivatives of $f$ satisfy $|f|_m\le C'_m A_f\mathsf D^m$, with $A_f\ge0$ and an arbitrary real normed target space.

For every $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, summing the derivatives with weights $\ell_*^m$ gives $\|c\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C$ and $\|f\circ X\|_{[n]}\le C_n A_f$. Here the formal derivative norm is the operator norm of the full multilinear derivative, whereas the paper sums coordinate derivatives; finite-dimensional comparison only changes the order-dependent constants. One integer $C$ and the coefficient constants are chosen before the parent and the derivative order. The composition constants may depend on the prescribed sequence $C'_m$, as the paper permits. The transported covector is nonzero, so the displayed divisions are ordinary divisions. The stronger verdict concerns the larger parent-pressure class; it does not assert a better power of $\lambda$.

lean.plain: Scaled derivative bounds for the parent coefficients
